findings.detail: 9 questions open with the same sentence (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19): "Name the change of state when ice becomes liquid w"
9 questions open with the same sentence (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20): "Describe how the particles are arranged in liquid "

issues.label: 1a, 2a, 3a, 4a, 5a, 6a, 8a, 9a, 10a
issues.detail: Identical question repeated 9 times across all 10 assessment items. Questions 1a–6a and 8a–10a all ask 'Name the change of state when ice becomes liquid water' with identical marking criteria and model answers. This violates assessment design principles requiring question variety.
issues.correction: Replace repeated questions with varied content: e.g., 'Name the change of state when liquid water becomes steam' (boiling), 'Name the change of state when steam becomes liquid water' (condensation), 'Name the change of state when ice becomes steam directly' (sublimation), or questions about other materials/processes within Topic 2.

issues.label: 1b, 2b, 3b, 4b, 5b, 6b, 8b, 9b, 10b
issues.detail: Identical question repeated 9 times. Questions 1b–6b and 8b–10b all ask 'Describe how the particles are arranged in liquid water compared with ice' with identical marking criteria and model answers. No variation in content or progression.
issues.correction: Replace with varied questions: e.g., 'Describe particle arrangement in steam compared with liquid water', 'Explain why ice floats on water using particle arrangement', 'Compare particle movement in ice, liquid water, and steam', or questions on other materials (metals, gases, polymers) from Topic 2.

issues.label: 7a, 7b
issues.detail: Question 7 introduces boiling/steam but lacks context connection to earlier questions. Assessment does not progress logically from melting (questions 1–6) to boiling (question 7). No intermediate questions on condensation or other state changes.
issues.correction: Restructure assessment with logical progression: melting (ice→water), then boiling (water→steam), then reverse processes (condensation, freezing). Alternatively, integrate question 7 earlier or add questions on all state changes systematically.

review.summary: Assessment contains severe repetition: questions 1a–6a and 8a–10a are identical (melting), as are 1b–6b and 8b–10b (particle arrangement comparison). Nine of twenty questions are duplicates. Question 7 introduces new content (boiling) without logical progression. Requires substantial restructuring to provide content variety and coherent learning progression within Topic 2.
